summary.text: CA9 is the candidate with the strongest and most consistent convergent evidence. It is the top gene of the overall convergence ranking, and its rise in tumours is seen at protein level (log2FC [gene=CA9; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.269]) and replicates in TCGA-KIRC RNA (log2FC [gene=CA9; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=9.712]). Single-cell data place almost all tumour CA9 transcripts in the ccRCC cells themselves (share [gene=CA9; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.976]), so the bulk signal is tumour-intrinsic and not infiltration. CA9 is a surface antigen with a phase 3 antibody (girentuximab) and imaging literature, which makes it a target for antibody, radioligand and imaging use and a diagnostic biomarker. It is not a dependency: DepMap shows no ccRCC requirement, TCGA survival shows no prognostic signal, and the GTEx vital-organ proteome flags stomach enrichment as an on-target off-tumour concern.

A second group of surface antigens is supported by omics and existing drug programmes but carries specific safety or attribution caveats. CD70 is up at protein level, replicates in TCGA, has antibody and ADC programmes up to phase 2 and shows no vital-organ proteome enrichment (max TS [gene=CD70; type=normal_proteome; source=DATASET:GTEX-PROTEOME; vital_protein_ts_max=0.34]). However, one single-cell dataset attributes most of its transcripts to T/NK cells rather than tumour cells, so part of its bulk signal is immune. ENPP3 has an ADC history (AGS-16C3F) but stains strongly in normal kidney ([gene=ENPP3; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; kidney_staining_level=3.0]). SCARB1 tops the target profile and its protein rise replicates in the confirmatory cohort (log2 fold change [gene=SCARB1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=2.334]), but it has no literature support in this corpus and adrenal enrichment in the normal proteome. Its cell source also differs between single-cell datasets.

The strongest biomarkers fall into two kinds. NNMT is a tumour-intrinsic metabolic enzyme whose protein rise replicates in the confirmatory cohort (log2 fold change [gene=NNMT; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=4.776]). Higher expression goes with worse TCGA survival (log HR per SD [gene=NNMT; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=0.301]), and one ccRCC study agrees, so NNMT is a prognostic biomarker with a weak target case. PSAT1 and PCK1 are the most robust genes of the biomarker profile. Both are lost in tumours, reflecting the loss of normal tubule identity, and the loss replicates at protein level in the confirmatory cohort (PCK1 log2 fold change [gene=PCK1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-4.819]). By contrast, HK2, a top-ten target-profile gene, does not replicate at protein level in that cohort (log2 fold change [gene=HK2; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-0.256]).

Because the convergence ranking rewards literature and existing drugs, little-studied genes come from the separate discovery screen. Two tumour-cell genes are identified and prioritised for experimental validation. COL23A1 is made by ccRCC cells, replicates in TCGA and stays strongly up when extrapolated to a pure tumour (log2FC [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; rna_lfc_at_purity1=4.88]). It is annotated as a membrane protein, but its surface call rests on UniProt alone, and it has no adverse survival signal and no selective dependency. Its next tests are surface staining of tumour and normal tissue and a check of how evenly tumour cells express it. RAB42 is also tumour-cell derived, replicated and purity-robust, but it is an internal protein, so it would need a small-molecule or degrader route and a knockdown study to show that tumour cells need it. In the stroma track, the fibroblast gene OLFML2A replicates and persists at purity one. The top immune-track gene, MILR1, is infiltration-driven: its rise largely disappears in a pure tumour. None of these genes has been shown to matter for patients. Here novel means few ccRCC papers and no clinical drug.

Several results cut across all candidates. No top-ranked antigen or biomarker is a selective ccRCC dependency in DepMap. EPAS1 (HIF-2 alpha, the target of the approved drug belzutifan) has the most selective profile ([gene=EPAS1; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; selectivity=0.3]), but it is not statistically significant, and EPAS1 is mostly endothelial in single-cell data. SCD is up in tumours, but ccRCC lines show no selective sensitivity to its inhibitors in PRISM (BH q [gene=SCD; type=prism_response; source=DATASET:PRISM-20Q2; padj=0.932]). In the treatment trials (IMmotion150 and the CheckMate nivolumab-versus-everolimus trial), no gene separates the arms after correction: for CA9 the between-arm adjusted p is [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.difference_between_arms.padj=0.917]. Most candidates are therefore antigen, imaging or biomarker cases rather than functional vulnerabilities.

validation.text: The independent layers strengthen some candidates and weaken others. In the CPTAC confirmatory DIA cohort, protein rises replicate for NNMT (log2 fold change [gene=NNMT; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=4.776]), SLC16A3 (log2 fold change [gene=SLC16A3; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=3.551]) and SCARB1. Protein losses replicate for PSAT1 (log2 fold change [gene=PSAT1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-3.946]) and PCK1. Two calls do not replicate. HK2 protein does not rise in that cohort (adjusted p [gene=HK2; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_padj=0.074]), so its target-profile rank rests on RNA and one cohort. PPP1R1A protein loss has the right direction but is not significant (adjusted p [gene=PPP1R1A; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_padj=0.17]). CA9, CD70, FABP6 and DUSP9 had too few matched pairs to test, which is not a failure to replicate.

TCGA-KIRC replicates the tumour-versus-normal direction for all leading candidates. Only NNMT, ALDH6A1, PPP1R1A, PSAT1 and ALDOB carry a TCGA prognostic signal, and CA9, CD70 and SCARB1 do not. VHL and PBRM1 are the recurrent somatic drivers, but they are lost tumour suppressors, not druggable targets. No leading candidate is a selective ccRCC dependency in DepMap. PRISM adds a negative result: SCD is up in tumours, yet ccRCC lines are not selectively sensitive to SCD inhibitors (selectivity [gene=SCD; type=prism_response; source=DATASET:PRISM-20Q2; selectivity=0.019]), and the CA9 PRISM signal comes from a multi-target compound and is uninformative. PRISM uses 2D culture, which misses HIF-2 biology. The purity check separates tumour-intrinsic changes (CA9, CD70, NNMT, SCARB1, COL23A1 all survive extrapolation to a pure tumour) from infiltration (the MILR1 rise vanishes). Protein-adjusted kinase activity was not assessed for these candidates in this run.

robustness.text: Under random re-weighting of the target profile, SCARB1, CA9, SLC16A3, CD70, NNMT, ENPP3 and FABP6 stay in the top ten in most draws, with narrow rank intervals. These are the robust target calls. HK2 and ANGPTL4 complete the top ten but leave it more often. SLC16A3 and HK2 also drop out of the top twenty-five when the tumour-up omics stream is removed, so their position depends on that one stream. In the overall convergence ranking only CA9 and COXFA4L2 are robust top-ten genes. COXFA4L2 scores low on the target profile because it has no predicted tractability.

In the biomarker profile, PSAT1, PCK1 and SLC6A19 are the robust top-ten genes. ALDH6A1, PPP1R1A and NNMT reach the top ten in most draws but have wide rank intervals. SLPI, DUSP9, VWF and L1CAM depend on the chosen weights: SLPI and VWF leave the top twenty-five without the prognosis stream, and DUSP9 without the omics stream. The overall convergence score mixes target and biomarker evidence, so target calls here use the target profile and biomarker calls use the biomarker profile.

treatment.text: Two trials were examined: IMmotion150 (atezolizumab plus bevacizumab versus sunitinib) and the CheckMate nivolumab-versus-everolimus trial. In IMmotion150, higher CA9 is associated with longer benefit on sunitinib (log hazard ratio per SD [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.sunitinib.log_hr_per_sd=-0.336], adjusted p [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.sunitinib.padj=0.332]), and higher CD70 with longer benefit on atezolizumab plus bevacizumab (log hazard ratio [gene=CD70; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; log_hr_atezolizumab_bevacizumab=-0.383]). In the CheckMate trial, EPAS1 is associated with longer benefit on everolimus (log hazard ratio per SD [gene=EPAS1; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.everolimus_checkmate025.log_hr_per_sd=-0.183]). These are single-arm associations, not evidence of predictive value.

No gene separates the arms of either trial after correction. For CA9 the IMmotion150 between-arm adjusted p is [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.difference_between_arms.padj=0.917]. For NNMT (adjusted p [gene=NNMT; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.difference_nivolumab_vs_everolimus.padj=0.999]) and EPAS1 (adjusted p [gene=EPAS1; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.difference_nivolumab_vs_everolimus.padj=0.999]), the nivolumab-versus-everolimus difference is null. None of the candidates can yet be used to choose therapy.

subtypes.text: CA9 is a PBRM1 subgroup candidate: TCGA RNA is higher in PBRM1-mutant tumours (mutant minus wild-type [gene=CA9; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; PBRM1.tcga_rna.mutant_minus_wildtype_log2=1.148]) and lower in ccB than ccA ([gene=CA9; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; ccA_ccB.tcga_rna.ccB_minus_ccA_log2=-1.551]). A CA9-directed agent would therefore matter most in ccA and PBRM1-mutant tumours. PSAT1 is higher in BAP1-mutant tumours (mutant minus wild-type [gene=PSAT1; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; BAP1.tcga_rna.mutant_minus_wildtype_log2=1.711]) and in ccB ([gene=PSAT1; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; ccA_ccB.tcga_rna.ccB_minus_ccA_log2=2.364]). Its protein difference is not significant, so it is a subtype-marker lead, not a subgroup target. Subtype differences in bulk RNA can partly reflect different immune infiltration between subgroups. VHL, SETD2 and BAP1 subgroup effects were not examined for the other candidates.

adc.text: Among the known-target controls, CD70 has the best conjugate suitability ([gene=CD70; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.746]) and no vital-organ proteome enrichment, but it lacks Human Protein Atlas staining data, so normal-tissue safety is unconfirmed. CA9 scores lower (suitability [gene=CA9; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.647]) because of high stomach staining and proteome enrichment (tissue-specificity [gene=CA9; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; vital_organ_protein_ts_max=5.19]). ENPP3 (suitability [gene=ENPP3; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.578]) stains strongly in normal kidney and duodenum, an on-target kidney-toxicity concern.

The data-driven targets fare worse as conjugate candidates. SCARB1 is a surface protein, but adrenal staining is high and the GTEx proteome flags adrenal enrichment (tissue-specificity [gene=SCARB1; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; vital_organ_protein_ts_max=5.08]). Only a small share of tumour cells express it in the weakest quarter of donors ([gene=SCARB1; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=7.1%]). SLC16A3 is expressed homogeneously ([gene=SLC16A3; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=43.7%] of tumour cells in the weakest quarter of donors). However, it stains strongly in adrenal ([gene=SLC16A3; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; vital_organ_staining_level=3.0]), its short extracellular sequence limits antibody access, and the CSPA surfaceome did not observe it. NNMT is an intracellular enzyme, so a conjugate is not the route. These scores rank accessibility and staining; they do not show that a conjugate would work.

immune.text: Immune cells contribute a large share of CD70 tumour transcripts ([gene=CD70; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; immune_cell_share_of_tumour_transcripts=0.654]), so its bulk signal mixes tumour-cell and T-cell expression, consistent with the single-cell disagreement. VWF is the opposite control. It is not an immune-cell transcript (immune share [gene=VWF; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; immune_cell_share_of_tumour_transcripts=0.016]) and correlates negatively with the immune score ([gene=VWF; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; rho_with_immune_score=-0.369]). VWF therefore tracks vascular, immune-cold tissue. CD74 and CXCR4 are immune-cell genes whose bulk levels track hot, infiltrated tumours. The immune discovery genes MILR1 and LILRB4 are infiltration markers of macrophage abundance rather than tumour-cell targets.

cells.text: CA9 is the clearest tumour-intrinsic candidate. ccRCC cells hold almost all of its tumour transcripts (share [gene=CA9; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.976]), and paired tumour cells exceed proximal tubule by a wide margin (log2FC [gene=CA9; type=sc_tumor_vs_pt; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; log2fc=7.739]). The bulk signal is therefore not an infiltration artefact.

Two bulk candidates have a mixed cell source in the second single-cell dataset. CD70 is mainly tumour-cell in the Zhang dataset (share [gene=CD70; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); zhang2021_tumour_cell_share=0.964]), but T/NK cells dominate in the Li dataset (tumour-cell share [gene=CD70; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); li2022_tumour_cell_share=0.345]). SCARB1 is myeloid-dominant in Li (tumour-cell share [gene=SCARB1; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); li2022_tumour_cell_share=0.336]) and tumour-dominant in Zhang (share [gene=SCARB1; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); zhang2021_tumour_cell_share=0.582]), so its tumour-intrinsic call is uncertain. NNMT, in contrast, is assigned to tumour cells in both datasets (tumour vs tubule log2FC in Li [gene=NNMT; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); li2022_tumour_vs_tubule_log2fc=9.132]). MET is also mostly tumour-cell (RCC share [gene=MET; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.935]).

Several well-known ccRCC genes are not tumour-intrinsic. KDR is endothelial (endothelial share [gene=KDR; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Endothelial; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.951]), a microenvironment target for anti-angiogenic drugs. EPAS1 is mostly endothelial in this dataset (share [gene=EPAS1; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Endothelial; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.365]), with only a small RCC share (share [gene=EPAS1; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.051]), although dropout may hide some tumour expression. CD74 is mainly macrophage (share [gene=CD74; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Macrophage; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.436]) and CXCR4 mainly CD8 T cell (share [gene=CXCR4; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=CD8_T; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.563]), so bulk rises of these genes reflect infiltration.

spatial.text: In Visium sections, high-CA9 spots are significantly enriched for RCC neighbours and, more weakly, for macrophage neighbours. RCC carries nearly all composition-corrected in-situ CA9 expression. This is an abundance-weighted neighbourhood enrichment, not a ligand-receptor interaction. No other candidate received a spatial profile in this run.

structure.text: Structural context is a descriptive heuristic only. The AlphaFold model of CA9 has moderate overall confidence, and its top cavity (volume [gene=CA9; type=structural_context; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; volume_a3=126.8] cubic angstrom) is lined by confident residues with one accessible lysine. Detected cavities recover only about half of experimental ligand-contact residues. The discovery gene COL23A1 has a low-confidence model whose only cavity is tiny (volume [gene=COL23A1; type=structural_context; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; volume_a3=8.0] cubic angstrom), so the plausible route is an antibody against an extracellular domain. These cavity scores do not identify degrons, ligase compatibility or degradation, and this run cites no curated experimental degron or ternary-complex reference for any candidate.

discovery.text: COL23A1 leads the tumour-cell track of the discovery screen. ccRCC cells make it, the rise replicates in TCGA, and it grows stronger when extrapolated to a pure tumour (log2FC [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; rna_lfc_at_purity1=4.88]). It is novel in the sense used here: few ccRCC papers and no clinical drug. UniProt annotates it as cell membrane with low vital-organ RNA. However, SURFY calls it non-surface and the CSPA surfaceome does not detect it. TCGA shows no adverse survival, and DepMap shows no selective dependency. Before COL23A1 can be treated as an antibody target, its surface location, normal-tissue staining and homogeneity across tumour cells must be confirmed.

RAB42 is the second tumour-track gene. It is mostly RCC-derived, replicates in TCGA, stays up at purity one, has very few ccRCC papers and has no clinical drug. It is an internal protein and not antibody-accessible. It has no adverse-survival signal and no selective dependency, so a knockdown study in ccRCC models would be the first test of whether tumour cells need it.

The stroma and immune tracks need different interpretation. In the stroma track, the fibroblast-secreted OLFML2A replicates and persists at purity one (log2FC [gene=OLFML2A; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=stroma; rna_lfc_at_purity1=1.527]), but it has appreciable colon RNA. The endothelial Notch ligand JAG2 is replicated and purity-robust, with heart-muscle expression as a safety question. The immune pool is the largest, and its leaders are infiltration-driven. MILR1 is linked to adverse survival, but its rise collapses in a pure tumour (log2FC [gene=MILR1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=immune; rna_lfc_at_purity1=0.414]), so it marks macrophage abundance. LILRB4 behaves the same way (log2FC [gene=LILRB4; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=immune; rna_lfc_at_purity1=0.508]). GAL3ST4 is an internal macrophage enzyme. All of these are data-ranked hypotheses: none has a selective dependency.

literature.text: Literature support is strongest for the antigens, but it is early-stage. One study reports that CA9 is enriched in ccRCC cells with low background in normal kidney, and that CA9-targeted PET gives proof-of-concept discrimination of ccRCC that warrants prospective validation. Another describes CD70 as commonly overexpressed in RCC and minimal in normal tissue, with labelled single-domain antibody radiotracers under development. For NNMT, one ccRCC study links high expression to worse overall and disease-specific survival. The NNMT inhibitor literature is chemistry and shows no ccRCC efficacy. The COXFA4L2 (NDUFA4L2) and HILPDA papers describe HIF- and MYC-linked metabolic roles (ferroptosis suppression, lipid droplets) from cell and mouse work only.

For the down-regulated biomarkers the literature is mostly bioinformatic. ALDOB and SLC22A8 are each described as prognostic markers lost in tumours, with limited immunohistochemistry, and ENO2 as a glycolytic diagnostic and prognostic marker. MT1G is contradictory: it is reported low in ccRCC tissue, yet high MT1G is tied to advanced stage and to growth and metastasis, so its direction of effect is ambiguous. SCARB1 and PIGR rank highly on data but have no literature relation in this corpus. Their ranking therefore rests on omics, replication and Open Targets association alone.

external.text: Open Targets confirms antibody tractability with clinical programmes for CA9 (girentuximab at phase 3), CD70 (cusatuzumab at phase 2, other antibodies and an ADC at phase 1) and ENPP3 (the ADC AGS-16C3F at phase 2). UniProt places all three at the plasma membrane. EPAS1 is the established drug target (belzutifan is approved), and its DepMap profile is the most selective of the candidates ([gene=EPAS1; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; selectivity=0.3]), though not significant. CA9, CD70, NNMT and SCARB1 show no ccRCC dependency. For CD70 the selectivity is essentially zero ([gene=CD70; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; selectivity=0.006]), and NNMT knock-out has a positive mean effect ([gene=NNMT; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; mean_effect_ccrcc=0.316]). Open Targets lists no drug for SCARB1 or NNMT, and the COXFA4L2 entries (ME-344, metformin) are non-specific mitochondrial agents.

omics.text: Six tractable candidates are up in tumours in the CPTAC discovery cohort and replicate in TCGA. CA9 (protein log2FC [gene=CA9; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.269]) and CD70 (protein log2FC [gene=CD70; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.421]) are the antigen controls. The protein rise is larger for NNMT (log2FC [gene=NNMT; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.709]) and smaller for SCARB1 (log2FC [gene=SCARB1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=1.837]) and ENPP3 (log2FC [gene=ENPP3; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=1.544]). The lactate exporter SLC16A3 (MCT4) is up in RNA (log2FC [gene=SLC16A3; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-RNA; layer=rna; log2fc=3.435]) and protein, which fits the glycolytic HIF programme. All of these changes survive extrapolation to a pure tumour. In the GTEx vital-organ proteome, CA9 is stomach-enriched (TS [gene=CA9; type=normal_proteome; source=DATASET:GTEX-PROTEOME; vital_protein_ts_max=5.19]), whereas CD70 and ENPP3 show no vital-organ enrichment.

The leading down-regulated genes mark the loss of normal tubule identity and are prognostic in TCGA. PSAT1 protein is lower in tumours (log2FC [gene=PSAT1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=-1.963]). Low ALDH6A1 expression goes with worse survival (log HR per SD [gene=ALDH6A1; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=-0.554]), and frequent 14q loss with a positive cis effect points to a real dosage component. PPP1R1A is strongly lost, and higher residual expression goes with worse survival (log HR per SD [gene=PPP1R1A; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=0.403]). These genes are biomarkers, not targets. The phosphosite and kinase-activity layers were not explored by the omics specialist in this run.

integration.text: Omics, literature and external knowledge converge most clearly on CA9 and CD70. Both are tumour-up at protein level, replicated in TCGA, described in the ccRCC literature as tumour-selective antigens with imaging tracers, and backed by clinical-stage antibodies in Open Targets. NNMT is the clearest convergent biomarker: omics, TCGA survival and a dedicated ccRCC study all point to worse outcome with high expression. COXFA4L2 (NDUFA4L2) shows agreement between omics and preclinical literature on a HIF-driven mitochondrial role, but its drug links are non-specific metabolic agents. The streams disagree in three places. SCARB1 and PIGR rank in the convergence top ten on data alone and are silent in this literature corpus. MT1G is low in tumours, yet one study reports that high levels are oncogenic. And the external drug landscape (the approved HIF-2 inhibitor for EPAS1) is not reflected in RNA convergence, because EPAS1 acts at the protein and pathway level.

Sorted by role, the candidates fall into three groups. Targets are surface antigens suited to antibody, ADC, radioligand or cell-therapy delivery: CA9, CD70 and ENPP3 (all with drug programmes), plus SCARB1 and SLC16A3 as data-driven targets without ccRCC drugs. Biomarkers are mostly kidney-lineage genes lost in tumours (PSAT1, PCK1, ALDH6A1, PPP1R1A, ALDOB, SLC22A8) together with the tumour-up prognostic enzyme NNMT. The mechanism group holds the drivers VHL and PBRM1, mutated in large fractions of tumours (VHL [gene=VHL; type=somatic_recurrence; source=DATASET:SOMATIC-CPTAC-TCGA; freq=0.483]; PBRM1 [gene=PBRM1; type=somatic_recurrence; source=DATASET:SOMATIC-CPTAC-TCGA; freq=0.362]). These loss-of-function tumour suppressors explain the HIF programme behind CA9, NNMT and SLC16A3, and they are best used for stratification rather than as direct targets.

targets.rationale: Top of the overall convergence ranking and robust in the target profile. Tumour-intrinsic by single-cell data and purity, up at protein level, replicated in TCGA, a surface antigen with a phase 3 antibody and PET imaging literature. Main limitations: stomach enrichment in normal tissue, no dependency and no prognostic value.

Robust in the target profile, up at protein level, replicated in TCGA, with the best conjugate suitability and no vital-organ proteome enrichment, plus clinical antibodies and radiotracer literature. Main limitations: part of its signal comes from T/NK cells, there are no normal-tissue staining data, and it has no dependency.

Robust in both profiles. Tumour-intrinsic in both single-cell datasets, its protein rise replicates in the confirmatory cohort, and high expression predicts worse TCGA survival, in line with a ccRCC study. Classed as a biomarker rather than a target because it is an intracellular enzyme with no drug and a positive DepMap effect.

Most robust gene of the target profile, with its protein rise replicating in the confirmatory cohort. Ranked below CA9 and CD70 because it has no literature support in this corpus, its cell source differs between single-cell datasets, adrenal enrichment raises a safety concern, and few tumour cells express it in some donors.
Robust in the target profile. A membrane enzyme up at protein level and in TCGA, with an ADC in phase 2. Main limitation: strong staining in normal kidney and duodenum, an on-target toxicity concern.

Robust in the target profile, with its protein rise replicating in the confirmatory cohort, homogeneous tumour-cell expression and a fit with the glycolytic HIF programme. Main limitations: its rank depends on the tumour-up omics stream, its short extracellular sequence limits antibody access, adrenal staining is high, and it has no drug.

Most robust gene of the biomarker profile. Protein loss replicates in the confirmatory cohort, it is prognostic in TCGA, and it marks BAP1-mutant and ccB tumours. A loss-of-identity biomarker, not a target.
Robust in the biomarker profile, with protein loss and both measured phosphosites replicating in the confirmatory cohort. A loss-type biomarker with no target route.

Included despite a modest convergence rank because it is the approved drug target of belzutifan and has the most selective, though not significant, DepMap profile of the candidates. Main limitations: its RNA is not strongly differential, it is mostly endothelial in single-cell data, and no trial arm difference was found.

A robust top-ten gene of the overall ranking, strongly up and replicated in TCGA, with preclinical literature on a HIF-driven mitochondrial and ferroptosis role. Classed as a biomarker because it has no predicted tractability, its listed drugs are non-specific, and it has no dependency.
Down in tumours with a dosage component from 14q loss, and low expression predicts worse TCGA survival. Ranked lower because its biomarker-profile rank interval is wide.

Exploratory: the leading tumour-cell discovery gene, made by ccRCC cells, replicated in TCGA and purity-robust, with few ccRCC papers and no drug. Main limitation: its surface location rests on UniProt alone, and it has no adverse prognosis and no dependency.

Exploratory: a tumour-cell discovery gene, replicated in TCGA and purity-robust, with very few ccRCC papers. Main limitation: it is an internal protein that antibodies cannot reach, with no prognostic signal and no dependency.

limitations.text: FABP6 is a robust top-ten gene of the target profile and SLC6A19 of the biomarker profile, but no specialist examined either gene in this run, so they are left out of the target list for lack of verified evidence beyond the ranking. They should be reviewed in a follow-up.
HK2 is in the target-profile top ten but is not listed as a target because its protein rise does not replicate in the confirmatory cohort.

No candidate is a selective ccRCC dependency in DepMap or PRISM, so the target calls rest on expression, replication, tractability and safety profiles, not on demonstrated vulnerability. PRISM uses 2D culture and misses HIF-2 biology.
Treatment associations come from single trial arms of modest size; no gene separates the arms after correction, so none is a predictive biomarker.
Conjugate suitability scores rank accessibility, staining and homogeneity only. CD70 lacks normal-tissue staining data, and the GTEx proteome lacks kidney and has detection limits.

Single-cell attribution for CD70 and SCARB1 differs between the two datasets, and some cell groups (endothelium, fibroblasts, proximal tubule) have few cells or donors. Low EPAS1 detection in tumour cells may include dropout.

Literature support often rests on single studies in a small corpus (about three hundred abstracts). PIGR, a convergence top-ten gene, has no literature relation and was not reviewed further. MT1G is left out of the target list because the literature contradicts itself on its direction of effect.

Several highly ranked down-regulated genes (ALDOB, SLC22A8, UMOD, FABP1) mark loss of proximal-tubule identity and may partly reflect tissue composition despite purity adjustment. They suit biomarker use only.

The phosphosite and kinase-activity layers, protein-level survival, and the VHL, SETD2 and BAP1 subgroup effects for most candidates were not examined in this run. Structure scores are descriptive heuristics of predicted monomers and are not evidence of a degron or degrader.
Discovery candidates are data-ranked hypotheses. Novel means at most a few ccRCC papers and no clinical drug, and nothing here shows that targeting them would help a patient.
